issues.display_title: Issue #59: Investigate Application Freeze on Upload Form Submission
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

A user reported that the application halts completely ("program stops total") right after filling in the name and location fields and initiating upload.

Result by developer

🔍 Investigation Findings: Potential Causes for Application Freeze

Based on the investigation into the upload flow, here are the likely causes of the freeze right after submitting:

1. File Contention Caused by Form Field Unfocusing (Most Likely)

When clicking Start Upload, the form fields (Tour Name and Address) are immediately disabled. Disabling an active field forces it to lose focus (blur event), which inadvertently triggers an extra save process for the tour details.

Because this extra save happens at the exact same second the background upload job begins writing tour information to the project files, Windows encounters a file-sharing conflict. The app tries repeatedly to access and rename locked files on the main thread, causing the desktop window to freeze or enter a "Not Responding" state.

2. Missing Submission Guard on "Start Upload" Button (High Chance)

The upload button does not lock immediately upon the first click because it waits for the initial save to complete first. If a user double-clicks or clicks the button again while it is preparing, two separate upload processes are launched for the same project simultaneously. These two tasks then collide over the same project files and images, leading to a freeze or crash.

3. Missing Configuration File in Windows Release Builds (Medium Chance)

The Windows release installer currently does not bundle a required configuration file (myconfig.config) used during the photo GPS tagging step. In installed versions, when the app reaches the photo processing stage, the background tool cannot locate this file, which may cause the process to stall or fail abruptly.

✅ Update: Fix Implemented & Verified

The fixes addressing the application freeze on upload submission have been implemented and successfully verified.

Summary of Changes:

  1. Immediate Button Lock: The "Start Upload" button now disables immediately on the first click, preventing rapid double-clicks from launching duplicate upload tasks for the same project.
  2. Prevented Background Save Contention: Disabling the input fields during upload initiation no longer triggers an unintentional background save, eliminating the file conflict on Windows that previously caused the app to enter a "Not Responding" state.
  3. Upload Guard per Project: Added a safeguard to guarantee only one active upload process can run for a specific project at a time.
  4. Included Missing Configuration File: Added the necessary configuration file (myconfig.config) into the application release bundle so photo processing and GPS tagging proceed without errors.

issues.display_title: Issue #60: fix(auth): SSO login stores wrong user id and token, so uploads fail with 401
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Problem

After signing in with GoThru Keycloak SSO, every upload fails with the toast Upload Failed: authentication required (SbError::Unauthenticated, mapped from an HTTP 401 on /video/app/new_tour). Manual and Google login are not affected.

Root cause

Two wrong values were stored in the session after SSO login:

  1. User id. keycloak-login returns only messages, token and cookie (no user_id). GET /users/detail returns an encrypted payload, which the code ignored. handleCallbackUrl then fell back to the Keycloak sub claim (a UUID, e.g. c755d2ac-...). The legacy endpoints need the numeric GoThru user id.
  2. Token. login_sso stored the JWT from keycloak-login (claims: email, iat, exp, date_created) as the GoThru token. The legacy /video/app/* endpoints reject it. Manual and Google login store the shared application token from GET /auth/{local_token} via finish_login; the SSO path never called it.

Fix

  • src/features/auth/services/keycloak.ts
    • Add decryptGothruResponse() (PBKDF2-SHA512, 999 iterations, then AES-256-CBC; passphrase derived from ls and e4). Ported from gothru-photo-studio-tauri/src/utils/decryptResponse.ts.
    • fetchGothruUserId decrypts /users/detail and reads data.user_id.
    • Keep the Keycloak-claim fallback only as a logged warning.
  • src-tauri/src/commands/auth.rs: login_sso is now async, takes only gothru_uid, and calls auth::finish_login so the session holds the shared application token.
  • crates/sb-core/src/auth/mod.rs: finish_login is now pub.
  • src/shared/api/commands.ts: loginSso(gothruUid).
  • Test: round-trip test for decryptGothruResponse in src/features/auth/__tests__/keycloak.test.ts.

Verification

  • cargo check, tsc --noEmit, vitest (127 passed)
  • Manual: log out, log in via SSO, confirm the header shows a numeric id, then run an upload end to end
  • Confirm the session expiry now comes from the server (date_expired) and that session restore on relaunch works

Follow-ups

  • Ask the GoThru backend team to return user_id in keycloak-login, which would remove the decrypt step.
  • The decrypt test only proves the implementation is self-consistent; it was not checked against a server-generated fixture.
  • tests/e2e/workflow.spec.ts is picked up by vitest and fails (Playwright spec); unrelated to this change.
